<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="שבט_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518917075_theRebbe_40" batchId="meluket-_D7_A9_D7_91_D7_98_meluket__BH_POST_1766518917075_theRebbe_40__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>It is known that at the Giving of the Torah, the power for all service was granted, and the superiority of service, especially transforming darkness to light, is itself empowered by that original drawing down.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, it is known that at the Giving of the Torah, the power was given for the entire matter of service.</t>
    <t s="2">For although the drawing down that comes through service,</t>
    <t s="3">and all the more so through the service of transforming darkness into light,</t>
    <t s="4">has an advantage over the drawing down that was</t>
    <t s="5">(in actuality)</t>
    <t s="6">at the Giving of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="7">this very thing—that through service they are able to draw down these influences—</t>
    <t s="8">is [empowered] by the force of the drawing down that was at the Giving of the Torah.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The superiority of the drawing down through service was already potentially present in the Giving of the Torah, because it followed Yisro's acknowledgment, which introduced the advantage of light from darkness.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it may be said,</t>
    <t s="1">that this—that in the drawing down of the Giving of the Torah there was</t>
    <t s="2">(potentially)</t>
    <t s="3">also the superiority of the drawing down through service, and also the superiority of the advantage of light that comes from darkness—</t>
    <t s="4">is</t>
    <t s="5">because the drawing down of the Giving of the Torah was after Yisro said,12</t>
    <t s="6">"Now I know that the L-rd is greater than all the gods,"</t>
    <t s="7">as it is brought in the Zohar,13</t>
    <t s="8">that by Yisro acknowledging and saying, "Now I know that the L-rd is greater, etc.," the Holy One, blessed be He, was elevated and glorified14</t>
    <t s="9">in His supernal and lower glory, and afterward He gave the Torah.</t>
    <t s="10">And through this</t>
    <t s="11">(that the drawing down of the Giving of the Torah was after Yisro's acknowledgment)</t>
    <t s="12">an advantage was made</t>
    <t s="13">(so to speak)</t>
    <t s="14">in the Torah that was given at the Giving of the Torah</t>
    <t s="15">(even though it was given from Above)</t>
    <t s="16">in the manner of the advantage of light that comes from darkness.</t>
    <t s="17">However, at the Giving of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="18">since the giving of the Torah was from the side of Above</t>
    <t s="19">(and Yisro's acknowledgment was only a preparation for the Giving of the Torah),</t>
    <t s="20">the advantage</t>
    <t s="21">(so to speak)</t>
    <t s="22">in the Torah that was made through Yisro's acknowledgment was only potentially,</t>
    <t s="23">and through this the empowerment was drawn down,</t>
    <t s="24">that through the service of transforming darkness into light, there will be an advantage in the light</t>
    <t s="25">(also)</t>
    <t s="26">in actuality.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>To explain why Yisro's acknowledgment was needed before the Giving of the Torah, it is understood through the verse that the advantage of wisdom over folly is like the advantage of light from darkness, referring to the transformation of external wisdom into holiness.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And based on this, we can explain what is said in several discourses15</t>
    <t s="2">that in order to explain why before the Giving of the Torah, Yisro's acknowledgment was necessary,</t>
    <t s="3">this will be understood by prefacing what is stated,16</t>
    <t s="4">"And I saw that there is an advantage to wisdom over folly, as the advantage of light over darkness"</t>
    <t s="5">[For at first glance this is not understood,</t>
    <t s="6">and as the Zohar17 precisely asks,</t>
    <t s="7">"Why does it say, 'And I saw'?"</t>
    <t s="8">[King Solomon,</t>
    <t s="9">the wisest of all men,18]</t>
    <t s="10">for does not everyone know that there is an advantage to wisdom over folly?</t>
    <t s="11">And the explanation of this is19],</t>
    <t s="12">that the intention of "folly"</t>
    <t s="13">(here)</t>
    <t s="14">is</t>
    <t s="15">(not simple foolishness,</t>
    <t s="16">but rather)</t>
    <t s="17">external wisdoms, which are folly relative to the wisdom of the Torah.</t>
    <t s="18">And about this it says, "And I saw that there is an advantage to wisdom over folly, as the advantage of light over darkness,"</t>
    <t s="19">for just as the advantage of light is specifically from darkness,</t>
    <t s="20">for by darkness being transformed into light, an advantage is made in the light</t>
    <t s="21">(as is explained at length in the discourse series of the Hilula),</t>
    <t s="22">so too is it with wisdom</t>
    <t s="23">(the wisdom of the Torah)</t>
    <t s="24">and folly</t>
    <t s="25">(external wisdoms),</t>
    <t s="26">that through the refinement and transformation of the wisdom of the Other Side into holiness,</t>
    <t s="27">an advantage and addition is made in the wisdom of holiness.</t>
    <t s="28">And this is why before the Giving of the Torah, Yisro's acknowledgment was necessary,</t>
    <t s="29">for Yisro was a great sage in external wisdoms,</t>
    <t s="30">and by Yisro acknowledging that "the L-rd is greater than all the gods," the refinement of the wisdom of the Other Side was accomplished, being transformed into the wisdom of holiness,</t>
    <t s="31">and through this an advantage and addition was made in the wisdom of holiness,</t>
    <t s="32">higher than it is in its own right.</t>
    <t s="33">[And based on this, we can explain what our sages said,20</t>
    <t s="34">that the reason he is called "Yisro" is because he added (yiter) a portion in the Torah,</t>
    <t s="35">for at first glance, the name "Yeter" is also from the term "advantage" (yitron),</t>
    <t s="36">so why was he called "Yeter" before he added a portion in the Torah?</t>
    <t s="37">And according to the above, it may be said21</t>
    <t s="38">that the name "Yeter"</t>
    <t s="39">(from the term "advantage")</t>
    <t s="40">by which he was called previously, is due to the advantage and superiority of intellect,</t>
    <t s="41">for the advantage and superiority of intellect</t>
    <t s="42">(over the emotions)</t>
    <t s="43">exists also in the wisdom of the Other Side.</t>
    <t s="44">However, in the wisdom of the Other Side,</t>
    <t s="45">since it is the epitome of selfhood,</t>
    <t s="46">and the fall caused by the intellect of the Other Side is a greater fall than the fall caused by the emotions of the Other Side,22</t>
    <t s="47">its advantage is in the manner of what is said,23</t>
    <t s="48">"Anything extra is considered as if removed."</t>
    <t s="49">But after he converted and added a portion in the Torah, he is called "Yisro" with the addition of a vav,</t>
    <t s="50">for a vav alludes to the Torah,24</t>
    <t s="51">as it is brought in the Zohar25</t>
    <t s="52">that a vav is the letter of truth, and there is no26</t>
    <t s="53">truth except Torah,</t>
    <t s="54">to indicate that his advantage is</t>
    <t s="55">(not in the wisdom of the Other Side, but rather)</t>
    <t s="56">in the wisdom of the Torah].</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
